bull_bear.body:
- CRAR 20.07% (Tier1 18.68%, Tier2 1.39%) vs 19.94% Dec'25 — ample headroom cited as reason bank chose to
  prioritize advances growth over further capital conservation this year.
- PCR (ex-technical-write-off) raised to 65.39% (from 61.23% Dec'25); incl. TWO 83.54% (from 80.90%) — accelerated
  provisioning pace (+400bps in Q4 vs typical ~100bps/quarter) explicitly funded by the yield-linked income upside.
- Good dividend paid in FY26 (referenced by a retail-investor caller; amount not restated on this call).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **New Executive Director hired externally** after the post ~9-10 months vacant; an analyst raised the
  cultural-fit risk given last year's friction with external hires — management deflected specifics ("past is
  history, present is reality").
- **ECL transition:** ~1–1.5% net-worth impact phased over 4–5 years, ~25–30bps/year credit-cost drag — confirm
  actual quarterly credit-cost trajectory once ECL rules bite (RBI timeline).
- **Corporate-heavy incremental growth mix:** 65% of FY26 incremental advances came from corporate/mid-corporate,
  not RAM — retail/MSME build-out is management's stated priority but has structurally lagged so far.
- **Employee-cost/actuarial volatility:** management explicitly would not commit to an FY27 number; the Q4
  step-down may partially reverse.
- **Geopolitical (Middle East conflict) exposure to NRI/FCNR deposits:** management says the book is "not
  sizable," low risk, but flagged as an external swing factor on branch-expansion pace and margins generally.
- **Slippage sustainability:** Q4's ₹147cr slippage (vs ₹250–300cr run-rate) — watch whether this holds or reverts.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- MD Raghavendra Bhat (joined July 2025, mid a stated "management crisis" year) repeatedly emphasizes a
  turnaround narrative: advances had fallen from ₹78,000cr to ₹71,000cr before recovering to ₹83,340cr; frames
  FY26 as delivering on "every" guided metric from a year ago. Confident, combative tone with skeptical
  analysts ("you are not believing me... we will do it").
- Notably evasive/deferred-to-email on several specific quantifications: gratuity/actuarial cost breakdown,
  G-Sec vs T-bill book split (initially), FY27 employee-cost number, exact PCR end-target — a pattern of strong
  qualitative reassurance without hard numeric commitments beyond the headline ratios already guided.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The "second consecutive quarter of growth" (per an analyst) is explicitly a recovery from a self-admitted
  weak FY25 (advances degrew from ₹78,000cr to ₹71,000cr) — YoY comparisons on advances (₹78,000cr→₹83,000cr)
  understate the actual turnaround magnitude (₹71,000cr→₹83,000cr) that management prefers to cite.
- Bank has intentionally exited low-yield, opportunistic corporate/treasury-arbitrage lending (IBPC/Food
  Credit book down ~58% YoY) in favor of RAM — a genuine mix-shift, not just a headline number.
- Growth is now explicitly phased monthly, not quarterly: management cited a granular monthly growth
  bifurcation (5%/8%/9%/10%/14% across the year) with H1:H2 split of 39%:61%, reflecting the bank's own
  10-year seasonality pattern (growth historically concentrated in H2/Q4).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Medium-term "Targeted Performance" framework: "Consolidation of financial position to build stakeholder value and enhanced return on equity", with ROA 1.1% - 1.35% under "Effective Capital Allocation".
- Funding and deployment targets: CD Ratio 79.0% - 80.0% ("Optimize Mix"), CASA ~34.0% ("Stable Source of Funding"), NIM 3% - 3.4% ("Consistent Interest Margins").
- Asset-quality target of NNPA 0.6% - 0.8% ("Enhance Asset Quality"); CRAR stood at 21.10% in Q1FY27 (Tier 1 19.9%, Tier 2 1.2%) versus 18.0% in FY24.
- Ownership is fully dispersed with no shareholder above 5%: Indian Public 57.5%, Foreign Institutions 13.1%, Mutual Funds 8.6%, Body Corporate 8.1%, Insurance Companies 5.9%, HUFs/LLPs & Trusts 2.7%, NRIs 2.5%, Domestic Institutions 1.2%, Others 0.4%.

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 3.07% Q4FY26 vs 2.92% Q3FY26 vs 2.98% Q4FY25 — driven by RAM yield focus + CASA/retail-TD cost-of-funds
  optimization. Yield on advances 8.78% Q4FY26 vs 8.71% Q3FY26 (+7bps). Cost of funds 5.38% vs 5.46% Q3FY26
  (-8bps). FY26 full-year: yield on advances 8.94% vs guidance ~9% (marginal miss).
- Book mix disclosed under pressing from an analyst: base rate 0.31%, MCLR 5.59%, EBLR-linked-to-G-Sec 2.31%,
  EBLR-linked-to-T-bill ~55% (bulk of book), remainder legacy — no G-Sec-linked advances currently (a change
  from the earlier NIM-drag years when G-Sec-linked pricing lagged repo cuts).
- Employee cost fell sharply QoQ/YoY (below ₹300cr/quarter for first time in 13–14 quarters per an analyst) —
  management attributed to natural attrition/superannuation (~350–400/month retiring, replaced selectively) plus
  an unquantified actuarial-revaluation benefit tied to the yield move; declined to give FY27 employee-cost guidance.
- Cost-to-income improved sharply: Q4FY26 50.47% vs 58.72% Q3FY26; FY26 56.34% vs 60.11% FY25; FY27 target 52–53%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Highest-ever quarterly and annual PAT; NIM recovered to 3.07% (Q4); GNPA/NNPA at
  2.78%/0.98%; cost-to-income fell sharply to 50.47% (Q4); FY26 guidance largely delivered; FY27 guidance set

- _Q1 FY27 → check: whether Q4's low slippage (₹147cr) and cost-to-income (50.47%) were seasonal/one-off or hold;

  actuarial-linked step-down; ECL-transition credit-cost impact starting to show; RAM vs corporate mix shift;
  new Executive Director settling in._

outlook.body:
- **Overall business growth:** ~15% for FY27 (reaffirmed, "slow but steady, conservative").
- **Deposit growth:** 10–15%; **Advances growth:** 15–20%.
- **CASA:** maintain 33%+ of deposits.
- **CD ratio:** target 80% (was 76.61% in Q4FY26).
- **ROA:** "1% plus" (unchanged wording, no upgrade despite Q4 ROA of 1.27%).
- **Cost-to-income:** targeting 52–53% for FY27 (down from 56.34% FY26, 50.47% in Q4FY26 alone).
- **Employee expense:** expected broadly flat YoY vs FY26 (~₹1,500cr FY25-level referenced by an analyst) — no
  significant further reduction guided; management would not commit to a number.
- **NIM:** management believes NIM has "bottomed out" around current levels (~3%+); further improvement
  contingent on EBLR trajectory — no explicit numeric target beyond the existing "3%+" guidance.
- **PCR:** informal target of "+1% per quarter" continuing, though Q4 saw a 400bps jump; no fixed end-state % given.
- **Recovery from technically-written-off book (~₹2,500cr o/s):** management's stated (self-described
  "ambitious") aim is to recover ~50% of the NPA/technical-write-off book, but declined to give a year-specific number.
- **ECL transition:** estimated impact ~1–1.5% on net worth overall, phased over 4–5 years (~25–30bps/year credit-cost impact); capital adequacy (CRAR 20.07%) said to be sufficient to absorb it.
- **Branch expansion:** ~31 branches opened in FY26; FY27 plans intact but subject to "course correction" if
  geopolitical/macro conditions (Middle East conflict, oil prices) worsen — no firm branch-count guided.

deepdive.thesis:
Karnataka Bank posted its highest-ever quarterly PAT (₹408.19cr, +40% QoQ / +62% YoY) and highest-ever FY PAT
(₹1,310.50cr, +3% YoY) in Q4FY26, delivering on nearly every FY26 guidance metric management had given a year
earlier (business, deposits, CASA%, GNPA, NNPA, ROA, CD ratio) under new MD Raghavendra Bhat (joined July 2025
after a prior-year "management crisis"), driven by a sharp NIM recovery (2.92%→3.07% QoQ), NPA/slippage
improvement and a steep sequential cost-to-income drop (58.72%→50.47% QoQ) — though management was evasive on
quantifying how much of the cost improvement and other-income jump was one-off (actuarial/yield-linked employee
cost swing, technical-write-off recoveries, Q4 seasonal card fees) versus structural.

open.item: A ~Rs. 101 crore account slipped into restructured due to technical issues in Q2; expected to be resolved and reversed before end-November / December 15, 2025.
To launch an MSME digital portal (mobile access, value-added features) within about 2-3 quarters; budget approved.
To recruit about 400-600 people in FY26 (probationary officers and clerical), similar to or 20-30% above last year's 400+.
FY26 total establishment/employee cost expected to close at about Rs. 1,700 crores (from ~Rs. 1,538 cr), i.e. ~Rs. 200 cr normal increase.
Keep employee/other costs guarded via optimal use of staff (350-400 retiring monthly across the year) and IT-led automation, compensated by business growth.
Coming-quarter product launches: tobacco agri-input loans (tobacco board tie-up), programmable CBDC, NFC-based QR tap-and-pay, surrogate-based housing/mortgage loans, Dropline OD and LAP for MSME.
Continue consciously reducing low-yield bulk advances in favour of retail and mid-corporate growth; Rs. 2,000 cr sanctioned-but-undisbursed at March started disbursing post-April.
Ambitious aim to recover 50% of the NPA book and 50% of the technical write-off book (~Rs. 2,500 cr TWO pool).
NIM target of 3%+ for FY27 (FY26 3.07% in Q4, 2.88% full year); believed to have bottomed out.
ROA guidance of 1%+ for FY27, with an improving bias (Q4FY26 ROA 1.27%).

Major IT solutions planned for completion in FY27: loan origination system revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0; exploring AI for internal efficiencies.
FY27 business growth phased month-by-month with ~39% in H1 and ~61% in H2 (Q4-heavy), reflecting the bank's seasonality.
Maintain GNPA <3% and NNPA <1% (FY26 delivered GNPA 2.78%, NNPA 0.98%).
Cost-to-income targeted between 52% and 53% for FY27 (FY26 56.34%, Q4 50.47%).
Target CD ratio of 80% for FY27 (76.61% at March 2026).
Maintain CASA ratio at 33%+ during FY27.
FY27 advances growth targeted at 15% to 20%.
FY27 deposit growth targeted between 10% and 15%.
FY27 overall business growth targeted at around 15%.
Expected ECL guidelines impact of ~1%-1.5% overall, spread over 5 years (~25-30 bps per year); adequately capitalized to absorb it.

verdicts.item: Continue improving PCR (net of technical write-off) by at least 1% every quarter; PCR incl. TWO at 81.42%, excl. TWO at 58.18%.
verdicts.note: PCR excl technical write-off improved to 65.39% (+~400 bps in Q4); commitment exceeded.

verdicts.note: FY26 ROE 10.36% and ROA 1.05% below the 12-14%/1.1-1.2% ranges; strong Q4 exit (ROE 12.69%, ROA 1.27%). [±10% rule]
